note: The Action / Indicator Catalog. Weights are pre-committed: severity is fixed before we know who triggers an indicator. 'form' is 'condition' (a standing state of affairs -> LEVEL) or 'action' (a discrete move -> CHANGE). 'repeatable' indicators may fire multiple times so incremental captures accumulate. This same schema scores a future news event: an event is one 'action' indicator with a source and a date.

indicators.text: No independent judicial review of executive action exists.
Defy or ignore a binding court ruling.
Purge, pack, or forcibly retire judges to shape outcomes.
Strip courts of jurisdiction over a class of executive acts.
Route cases from independent courts to loyal special tribunals.
Curtail habeas corpus or core due-process guarantees.
Condition a single court's budget or appointments to pressure it.
Publicly threaten a specific judge over a pending ruling.
No competitive national election for the head of power exists.
Abolish or indefinitely postpone elections.
Remove or override term limits to extend own tenure.
Ban or disqualify a major opposition party or candidate.
Seize control of the election authority or alter the count.
Refuse or reverse a peaceful transfer of power.
Gerrymander or redraw districts to entrench a majority.
Raise registration or ballot barriers targeting opposition voters.
No independent mass media operates; information is state-controlled.
Shut down or nationalize an independent outlet.
Jail or prosecute a journalist for reporting.
Impose prior censorship or an internet / communications shutdown.
Force a critical outlet into allied ownership.
Use a libel or 'fake news' law to fine or silence a critic.
Condition one outlet's license, ad revenue, or access to shape its coverage.
Assembly, protest, and movement require state permission and are routinely denied.
Mass detention of civilians without trial.
Impose a state of emergency suspending civil rights.
Ban or violently disperse an opposition assembly or protest.
Criminalize a broad category of dissent (e.g. 'insulting the state').
Use foreign-funding or registration rules to shut down civil-society groups.
Surveil, harass, or administratively restrict a specific activist or NGO.
No legislature or judiciary is able to constrain the executive.
Dissolve the legislature.
Rule by decree, bypassing the legislature.
Invoke emergency powers beyond their lawful scope or duration.
Strip an oversight body (auditor, ombudsman, inspector) of independence.
Seize a subnational or federal power for the central executive.
Quietly expand a regulator's discretion to reward or punish firms.
The state routinely imprisons or kills for political reasons.
Systematic violence targeting an ethnic, religious, or political group.
Extrajudicial killing or forced disappearance.
Imprison a political rival or opposition leader.
Use torture in state detention.
Revoke citizenship or force a critic into exile.
Bring a selective prosecution to harass an opponent.
